verdict.reason: may interrupt a resource clients use by name (96%); the apply may fail part-way (97%)

state:
An OpenTofu (Terraform) plan is about to be applied to an AWS account (one region). Running applications use these resources by name: they read and write objects, table items, queue messages, secrets and parameters, and invoke functions. Applying the plan carries out the resource changes below in dependency order. Replacing a resource destroys the old one and then creates the new one, unless the plan says the new one is created first (create_before_destroy). If a change fails, the apply stops there; the changes already made stay made.

Current state:
aws_dynamodb_table.t: table vaws-s25-items (hash key pk, billing PAY_PER_REQUEST); holds 0 items; deletion protection off

Actions, in order:
1. Replace aws_dynamodb_table.t (destroy the old one, then create the new one, forced by the change to hash_key): attribute: [{name = "pk", type = "S"}] -> [{name = "id", type = "S"}]; hash_key: "pk" -> "id" [the name vaws-s25-items is already taken by an existing resource]

How these resources behave: Destroying an aws_dynamodb_table whose deletion protection is on fails, also when the same plan turns protection off for its replacement. A table created by a replacement starts empty: items are not copied. Creating a table whose name is already taken fails.

The questions are about the state after all these actions.
